evidence: Continue from Progress opens a blank content area with only bottom navigation rendered and Songs selected; no song, loading indicator, or error appears. The song opens from the Home Continue card. Reproduced twice on device after an eight-second wait.
recommendation: Open the selected song from Progress and show a loading or recoverable error state if it cannot be opened.

evidence: The optional autofill search is the first large field and resembles the required Title input. The CRUD flow initially entered the title there and received a Title required error.
recommendation: Clearly distinguish optional catalog search from manual entry and make the required Title field prominent.

evidence: Note names and tick marks around the dial are nearly white against pale gray and difficult to distinguish in the idle state.
recommendation: Use sufficiently contrasting colors for dial labels and markings in active and idle states.

evidence: Each row has two unlabeled dropdowns displaying a dash, and Original and Our do not clearly explain the versions. The adjacent selectors have small targets.
recommendation: Label root and quality controls, clarify the version names, and provide distinct targets of at least 48 × 48 dp.

evidence: The idle instruction says Tap Listen, but a top Listen control and a large microphone button are both visible; the accessibility tree reports two Listen controls. Auto, Manual, and note targets are small.
recommendation: Distinguish mode selection from starting detection and provide at least 48 × 48 dp targets.

evidence: Search has no accessible label, and repeated Metronome and More actions do not identify their songs.
recommendation: Label search and include song titles in accessible action labels.

evidence: Search and setlist rows are unlabeled clickable nodes, and repeated metronome and More actions do not identify their setlists.
recommendation: Label search and rows and include setlist names in action labels.

evidence: Band Name and Description are reported as unlabeled clickable nodes despite visible placeholders.
recommendation: Expose accessible labels and announce that Band Name is required.

evidence: Most visible history entries say Removed song without identifying information; some also say Unnamed sections, making sessions difficult to interpret.
recommendation: Retain readable song and section name snapshots and indicate when the source song is unavailable.

evidence: After transposing down, the control reads -1 while the header still displays Dm, leaving the sounding key and adjustment unit unclear.
recommendation: Label the adjustment in semitones and show the resulting key alongside the original.

evidence: The filter offers sharp note names only while song cards display flat keys such as Bbm and Ab, requiring users to infer enharmonic equivalents.
recommendation: Display equivalent sharp and flat names together and match both spellings.

evidence: Adjacent tag filter chips have touch targets shorter than 48 dp.
recommendation: Increase each chip's interactive height to at least 48 dp.

evidence: Play controls for available songs are unlabeled in the accessibility hierarchy and have small touch areas.
recommendation: Label each play action with its song title and enlarge its target to at least 48 dp.

evidence: Bottom navigation covers the lower part of the filter sheet, including the BPM selector.
recommendation: Place the sheet above navigation or provide enough bottom inset and scrolling.

evidence: The song title is truncated in both the header and bottom bar, so the full title cannot be read on the detail screen.
recommendation: Allow the title to wrap or provide another visible way to read it.

evidence: Tightly packed session names run into duration information or truncate when metadata is longer.
recommendation: Give names and metadata separate flexible regions and allow wrapping.

evidence: Section cards use colored borders to distinguish categories, but repeated labels such as Solo have no accompanying category marker or legend.
recommendation: Where border colors convey meaning, pair them with a text label, icon, or other non-color cue.

evidence: The card says Tap to start but opens Progress, where starting practice requires another action; More calls the destination Progress / history.
recommendation: Label the card as a route to progress or make its stated start action lead to practice, and name the destination consistently.

evidence: Icons for Key & BPM, Links, Song Structure, and Notes change when their sections expand.
recommendation: Keep identifying icons consistent and use a consistent expansion indicator.

evidence: The orange Record button is markedly rounder than the orange creation buttons; the theme specifies a 12px radius for filled buttons.
recommendation: Use the shared primary button shape and label treatment.
